title: test-0095-MAT-INTEGERS
passage: Rohan runs a small fruit stall in his village market. To keep his business organized, he uses a ledger to track his daily transactions. When he buys stock, he records the cost as a negative number to represent money leaving his pocket. For instance, when he bought a crate of apples for 500 rupees, he wrote -500 in his ledger. Later, he sold some apples and earned 300 rupees, which he recorded as +300. At the end of the day, his ledger showed -500 + 300, which equals -200, meaning he still needs to recover 200 rupees to break even. Sometimes, he receives a refund from a wholesaler for damaged goods. If he gets a refund of 100 rupees, he subtracts the negative cost, which is written as -(-100), resulting in a gain of 100 rupees. Rohan also tracks the temperature of his cold storage unit. If the temperature is -5 degrees and it drops by another 5 degrees, the new temperature is -10 degrees. He knows that -10 is colder than -5 because it is further to the left on the number line. Even though he deals with negative numbers, he knows they represent real-world values like debt or freezing temperatures, not just the act of subtraction.
summary: At the end of the day, his ledger showed -500 + 300, which means he still needs to recover 200 rupees. If he gets a 100-rupee refund, he subtracts the negative cost, which is written as -(-100), resulting in a gain of 100 rupees.
